import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 62

Let $p$ be a large prime, and let $A$ be the set of all primes less than $p$.
Is every $x \in \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$ congruent to some product $a_1 a_2$ where $a_1, a_2 \in A$?

This is a problem of Erdős, Odlyzko, and Sárközy [105] from 1987.

*Reference:* [Ben Green's Open Problem 62](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.62)
-/
open Filter
namespace Green62

/--
Let $p$ be a large prime, and let $A$ be the set of all primes less than $p$.
Is every $x \in \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$ congruent to some product $a_1 a_2$ where $a_1, a_2 \in A$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem green_62 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ᶠ p in atTop, p.Prime →
        let A := (Finset.range p).filter Nat.Prime
        ∀ x : ℕ, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < p →
          ∃ a₁ ∈ A, ∃ a₂ ∈ A, (x : ZMod p) = (a₁ * a₂ : ZMod p) := by
  sorry

end Green62

findings.description: The module docstring’s reference number `[105]` for the 1987 Erdős–Odlyzko–Sárközy paper is stale relative to the linked Green PDF. In its current bibliography, that paper is [113], while [105] is an unrelated paper by Erdélyi on unimodular zeros. The theorem and the author/year attribution are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: The linked Green list, Problem 62 (p. 30), attributes the problem to “Erdős, Odlyzko and Sárközy [113] from 1987.” Its bibliography (p. 53) identifies [113] as “On the residues of products of prime numbers,” Period. Math. Hungar. 18 (1987), 229–239, and [105] as Erdélyi’s 2016 paper. https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.62
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the mutable reference number with a stable author-year citation and the full bibliographic reference or direct paper URL, https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-22.pdf. Alternatively, update [105] to [113] for the currently linked PDF.

reformulations.difference: The primary literature also formulates this conjecture using all reduced residue classes and prime factors at most p. Lean uses natural representatives satisfying 1 ≤ x < p and factors strictly below p, and expresses sufficiently large primes through eventuality at atTop on ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For prime p, the integers 1,…,p−1 represent exactly the reduced residue classes. In a representation of a nonzero residue with factors at most p, neither factor can equal p, since that would make the product zero modulo p; thus the strict factor bounds are equivalent. Equality of natural-number casts in ZMod p is ordinary congruence modulo p, and casting preserves multiplication. Finally, eventually_atTop is equivalent to existence of a cutoff P beyond which the property holds for every prime p, uniformly over x. These equivalences were proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, including threshold_iff, covers_reduced_iff, and literature_iff.

review.notes: The sole theorem is mathematically faithful. The answer slot is a correctly scoped Prop-valued yes/no question. Prime hypotheses exclude the exceptional ZMod 0 and ZMod 1 cases, and primes exceed every cutoff, so the eventual prime implication is not vacuous. Finite tests covered all primes below 100; the pointwise property fails at p = 2, 3, 5 and holds at p = 79, consistently with the asymptotic question. The scratch file compiles successfully; its equivalence proofs use only standard Lean axioms. Green’s update concerns three factors, and Matomäki–Teräväinen explicitly say the two-factor conjecture remains open, even under GRH. No repository files were modified.
